courses.description: This course will introduce students to the recent research and debate regarding neural plasticity and the ability of the healthy adult brain to change. courses.description: Provides an introduction to the structure and function of the nervous system. Fundamental principles will be introduced including nervous system anatomy; molecular and cellular properties of the nervous system; sensory and motor systems; current methods used in neuroscience; and how the nervous system produces behavior and cognition. This course provides greater breadth and depth of neuroscience topics, as compared to Biopsychology ( PSYC 220 ). Previously offered as PSYC 175 and 315. Honors version available.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Human Neuroscience through Imaging and Data Science
courses.description: This Course-based Undergraduate Research Experience introduces students to big data approaches in human neuroscience, emphasizing neuroimaging methods such as fMRI, DTI, EEG, and PET, alongside behavioral measures. Throughout the semester, students will engage in original research analysis & visualization, working on a sustained, scaffolded research project and learn fundamental techniques in data preprocessing, statistical modeling, connectivity analysis, and visualization. The course also provides an accessible introduction to advanced approaches, including machine learning and network analysis. Students will work with publicly available neuroscience datasets, gaining practical experience analyzing large-scale data, and completing a project that applies big data methods to neuroscience.

courses.title: Cellular Mechanisms in Addiction Lab
courses.description: Cellular Mechanisms in Addiction is a laboratory and research-based course aimed at investigating the cellular underpinnings of drug addiction. Students will gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge approaches utilized in addiction research. Utilizing rodent brain tissue and immunohistochemistry techniques, students will delve into the cellular and molecular changes associated with addiction. Students may receive credit for only one NSCI 27X course. Majors only.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Brain Organoid Electrophysiology Lab
courses.description: This is a hands-on, course-based undergraduate research experience (CURE) in developmental neurobiology. Students learn the principles of early neurodevelopment and activity-dependent plasticity while gaining technical experience in sterile cell culture, brain organoid generation, and electrophysiological recording. Working in research teams, students design and execute an original experiment testing how environmental, pharmacological, or activity-based interventions influence neural activity during development. The course emphasizes experimental design, data collection and analysis, scientific reading, and communication through journal clubs, research manuscripts, and poster presentations. Students with credit for NSCI 270 -279 may not enroll.

By synchronizing EEG recorded on the scalp with experimental events, Event-Related Potentials (ERPs) link human brain activity to specific mental processes. Students will gain technical skills, through hands-on experience, in processing, analyzing, and interpreting electrophysiological data. Majors only.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Neural Circuits & Behavior
courses.description: This hands-on laboratory course introduces students to neuroscience research through a Course-Based Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) using Drosophila melanogaster. Students will investigate how neural circuits shape behavior by designing and conducting original experiments with behavioral assays and neural manipulation techniques (genetic, pharmacological, optogenetic). Emphasis is placed on collaboration, iteration, and scientific communication. Alongside their projects, students will analyze primary literature, develop hypotheses, troubleshoot challenges, and interpret novel data. The semester culminates in both a written research paper and a poster presentation, showcasing student-designed discoveries. Students may only receive credit for one NSCI 27X Lab CURE course.

Students will have the opportunity to delve into the effect of obesity and/or diabetes on the brain. In this course students will learn to handle rodent brains, perform cryostat sectioning, conduct reverse transcription, create a cDNA library, and utilize R programming to analyze qPCR results by studying genes of interest. courses.title: Advanced Molecular Neuropharmacology
courses.description: This course will examine the molecular basis of drug action in the brain. Students will learn about ligand-receptor interactions and modulation of receptor number, structure, and function by drugs. Detailed examples will examine the molecular details of both ligand-gated ion channels and G-protein coupled receptors. The course will use analysis of primary literature and a semester-long makerspace project to delve into research where central themes will include developing critical thinking, design thinking, and communication skills.

courses.title: Principles of Brain Circuits
courses.description: This course is designed for upper-level undergraduates who are interested in how brain circuits control behavior. A major focus will be the new technique of optogenetics that is revolutionizing our approach to systems neuroscience. Circuits that control movement, sensation, sleep, memory, and fear will be explored in detail. Points of emphasis will be circuits mediating pain as related to actions of opiates and circuits mediating feeding behavior as related to obesity.

courses.title: Emotion
courses.description: This course will provide a comprehensive overview of the scientific study of emotion. Topics will include theoretical models of emotion process and structure. A range of perspectives, including social, cultural, developmental, clinical, and cognitive psychology, as well as behavioral neuroscience, will be considered. Previously offered as PSYC 568.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, NSCI 175 or PSYC 101.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Neuropsychobiology of Stress
courses.description: Stress is a common experience in modern life that impacts psychological and physical health. In this course, we will delve into the scientific literature in psychology and neuroscience that explores how the brain and the body respond to stress, and how we can intervene to prevent stress from negatively impacting physical and mental health.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Honors in Neuroscience I
courses.description: This course comprises the first semester in the two-semester sequence of Senior Honors in Psychology/Neuroscience. There are two components to the course: research that you will conduct under the direction of your faculty thesis advisor, and this class, which you will attend with the other senior honors students to learn about research-related topics and receive consultations with the instructor and your classmates.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, A cumulative GPA of 3.3, at least one semester of PSYC/ NSCI 395 or the approved equivalent, and acceptance into the Psychology or Neuroscience Senior Honors Program; PSYC/ NSCI 693H must be taken in the first semester of the last year of studies.

courses.subject: NSCI
courses.title: Honors in Neuroscience II
courses.description: This course comprises the second semester in the two-semester sequence of Senior Honors in Psychology/Neuroscience. There are two components to the course: research that you will conduct under the direction of your faculty thesis advisor, and this class, which you will attend with the other senior honors students to learn about research-related topics and receive consultations with the instructor and your classmates. Admission to the neuroscience honors program required.
